name: turn-undead-first
description: Turn Undead intermediate checkpoint (planning/turn-undead/MISSION.md). Vanilla profile: the candidate alone, no other mod. In the loaded fixture save, a disposable cleric 5 / fighter 2 with Charisma 16 receives its real positive channel and the product's Turn Undead feat, then uses the granted cleric action through the game's ability command in real time against an ordinary skeleton and a zombie lord whose Will totals are lowered so they fail, a zombie lord whose Will is raised so it saves, a skeleton beyond 30 feet and a living hostile. The probe records the existing channel pool before and after, every saving throw and damage/heal rule on the tracked units, the product's persisted flight state, Frightened/panic and distances over two rounds, the intelligent round saves and a recovery after the zombie lord's Will is raised, and the mindless skeleton's unrefreshed one-minute expiry. Setup is disclosed in tools/LoaderCompatHarness/TurnUndeadProbes.cs. The same launch also runs the contracts extract (installed method IL hashes and blueprint values, every constructed Turn component checked against literal expectations), an undead channeler that must save against its own Turn beside a living control, and an abandoned first-turn probe whose release must restore the pause flag, every silenced brain and every spawned unit. A final step runs the abandon check through the harness's own probe slot three times (interrupted after its nested probe's first yield, cleanly and with an injected nested cleanup failure, and run to normal completion with the injected failure) and requires pause, brains, subscription and spawned-unit cleanup in every case, a restored isolation verdict only for the clean case, and refusal of the next probe after an unrestored one. Every target is judged from the save it actually rolled; an outcome the fixture aimed for but the dice did not produce is reported as incomplete coverage, not a product defect. A selective step casts once without and once with the native Selective Channel feat at an enemy and an allied (player-faction) skeleton: without it both are turned (all-undead behavior); with it only the enemy is turned and the ally rolls no save, matching the native harm channel rule. A last step checks the driver's own recording from outside through a further probe slot: a cleanup failure the driver does not expect, carried by its abandon child, must reach the driver's outcome as unrestored isolation when the driver is interrupted while it waits for deferred unit destruction, and must stop the driver before its next case when it continues.
